part.text:
Now I have the full picture:
- `financial.client` has `birth_date`, linked to `financial.district` via `district_id`
- `financial.district.A11` = average salary
- `financial.disp` links clients to accounts
- Younger = more recent (higher) `birth_date`

Let me run the query to find clients who are both youngest (max birth_date) AND in the district with highest average salary (max A11):

input.sql:
SELECT a.account_id
FROM financial.client c
JOIN financial.disp d ON c.client_id = d.client_id
JOIN financial.account a ON d.account_id = a.account_id
JOIN financial.district dist ON c.district_id = dist.district_id
WHERE c.birth_date = (SELECT MAX(birth_date) FROM financial.client)
AND dist.A11 = (SELECT MAX(A11) FROM financial.district)

SELECT MAX(birth_date) as max_birth, (SELECT MAX(A11) FROM district) as max_A11 FROM client

SELECT c.client_id, c.district_id, c.birth_date, d.disp_id, d.account_id, a.account_id as acct, dist.A11
FROM client c
JOIN disp d ON c.client_id = d.client_id
JOIN account a ON d.account_id = a.account_id
JOIN district dist ON c.district_id = dist.district_id
WHERE c.birth_date = (SELECT MAX(birth_date) FROM client) OR dist.A11 = (SELECT MAX(A11) FROM district)
LIMIT 30

JOIN district dist ON c.district_id = dist.district_id

SELECT DISTINCT a.account_id
FROM client c
JOIN disp d ON c.client_id = d.client_id
JOIN account a ON d.account_id = a.account_id
JOIN district dist ON c.district_id = dist.district_id
WHERE c.birth_date = (SELECT MAX(birth_date) FROM client)
   OR dist.A11 = (SELECT MAX(A11) FROM district)
ORDER BY a.account_id
LIMIT 200
